title: Prescribed components of normalized coefficient-pair descent
statement: Let $I$ be a directed preordered type, $C_i,D_i$ categories, and $S,T$ their stage systems, meaning transition functors with coherent associators on common-stage quotients as in [lem-sbc-coherent-pair-functor-descent]. Let $\phi_i:C_i\to D_i$ be functors with coherent comparisons $b_h:\phi_i T_h\cong S_h\phi_j$ in diagrammatic functor order. For each pair object $P$ and stage $M$ above its stage, suppose an isomorphism $c_{P,M}$ from the extended literal output pair to $\phi_M(P_M)$ has hom and inverse components heterogeneously equal to those of $b_h$ at $P$. Then there is exactly one descended functor with literal object $(i,\phi_i X)$ and representative arrow $[M,c_{P,M}\phi_M(a)c_{Q,M}^{-1}]$. This is only a conversion of the existing coefficient-pair functor specification to given equal components.

proof.text: Apply coefficientPairFunctor_exists. Its generic output equals the literal stagewise output pair. Destruct the two input pairs, turn the supplied component heterogeneous equalities into equalities, and rewrite the representative prescription in each direction. existsUnique_congr transfers the whole characterization and uniqueness.

lean.statement:
theorem existsUnique
    (b : ∀ {i j} (h : i ≤ j), φ i ⋙ T.T h ≅ S.T h ⋙ φ j)
    (hcoh : StageSystem.pairFunctorCoherent S T φ b)
    (c : ∀ (P : S.PairCategory) (M : I) (h : P.stage ≤ M),
      (object S T φ P).toStage h ≅ (φ M).obj (P.toStage h))
    (hc : ∀ (P : S.PairCategory) (M : I) (h : P.stage ≤ M),
      HEq ((b h).hom.app P.obj) (c P M h).hom ∧
        HEq ((b h).inv.app P.obj) (c P M h).inv) :
    ∃! F : S.PairCategory ⥤ T.PairCategory,
      (∀ P, F.obj P = object S T φ P) ∧
      (∀ (P Q : S.PairCategory) (M : I) (hP : P.stage ≤ M) (hQ : Q.stage ≤ M)
        (a : P.toStage hP ⟶ Q.toStage hQ),
        HEq (F.map (StageSystem.PairCategory.mkHom M hP hQ a))
          (StageSystem.PairCategory.mkHom
            (X := object S T φ P) (Y := object S T φ Q)
            M hP hQ ((c P M hP).hom ≫ (φ M).map a ≫ (c Q M hQ).inv)))
